label: Nebulae
description: A separately loaded overlay of the catalogued nebulae and supernova remnants within about 2000 ly, plus the remnants of the supernovae with recorded dates, rendered as approximate 3D volumes. Large H II regions take their sky shape from an all-sky H-alpha map; supernova remnants are modeled shells, except the Crab Nebula, whose filaments come from a measured 3D map.

cutoffPolicy: Every reflection nebula, H II region and planetary nebula that is listed in NGC/IC, van den Bergh, van den Bergh & Herbst, Sharpless, HASH, or in Lynds with a reflection-catalogue identification (Cederblad or Dorschner & Gürtler), spans at least 5 arcmin, and whose adopted distance is within 1 sigma of 2000 ly (distance - error <= 613.2 pc); the census is being added in reviewed batches, so it is not yet complete beyond 500 ly (153.3 pc). Distances come from the SIMBAD-adopted parallax (Gaia EDR3, else Hipparcos 2007) of the illuminating or central star; several stars use an inverse-variance mean, and Gaia DR2 cluster parallaxes or VLBA parallaxes of cluster members replace stars whose own parallax is unreliable or embedded. Sizes come from LBN for named NGC/IC nebulae, Sharpless for ionized nebulae, the SIMBAD-adopted angular diameter (or HASH radius) for planetary nebulae, twice the van den Bergh maximum radius in the north, and ESO/Uppsala or the van den Bergh & Herbst diameter south of the Lynds limit. H II regions larger than about 1 degree take their sky shape and relative brightness from the Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map. The Orion Nebula (about 1265 ly) was kept as a showcase beyond the earlier 500-ly cutoff. Excluded: dark nebulae and molecular clouds, nebulae under 5 arcmin, the possible planetary nebula FP J1912-0331, H-alpha-only ionized regions such as Spica's, and Barnard's Loop until its distance is settled (published estimates of about 170 and 440 pc disagree). Supernova remnants: those within 2000 ly whose distances are established (Vela, Monogem Ring, Hoinga), drawn as shells of their published size around their published centers; Antlia, the Gum Nebula and Vela Junior wait for settled distances or classifications. The Crab Nebula (about 6200 ly) is kept as a showcase beyond the cutoff, at the VLBI parallax distance of its pulsar. The remnants of the supernovae with recorded dates are added beyond the cutoff for the light-front topics: RCW 86 (SN 185, probable), RX J1713.7-3946 (SN 393, probable), SN 1006, Pa 30 (SN 1181), Tycho’s and Kepler’s remnants, Cassiopeia A (dated by its expansion) and SN 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud. 3C 58 (too old for SN 1181) and G11.2-0.3 (a doubtful match for SN 386) are left out.
